messages:
liam: heads-up - legal asked whether we can make sampling deterministic per-tenant to support chargeback while still redacting PII.

clare: do you mean deterministic sampling of requests for full capture, or deterministic hashing for telemetry buckets?

liam: full capture. some tenants want a consistent subset of traffic stored so their debugging traces line up. they also want PII redacted in stored logs.

roxana: risky if we store raw before redaction. proposal: compute a tenant-scoped HMAC(seed) to decide capture, then if captured, store redacted payload plus an encrypted blob (enterprise-only) that they can decrypt with their KMS. default hosted flow keeps encrypted blob disabled.

paul: sounds reasonable. implementation details: HMAC should be computed at the edge using tenant id + request-id so we can get stable sampling across retries. do not use request body plaintext in sampling decision (privacy).

liam: agreed. what about quotas? captured traces count against storage quota — need a UI to show expected capture rate per-route when you flip on deterministic sampling.

clare: console idea: route-level card with slider "capture rate (deterministic)" and a tiny estimate line: "est. traces/day: 3.2k". also show cost delta.

roxana: for telemetry heatmaps we still want signal from every request. suggest emitting a 64-bit footprint metric derived from a one-way hash of the body, but only as a metric label (no text). that gives distribution without leaking content.

paul: metric pipeline change: we already drop high-card labels. footprint must be low-card (e.g., 256 buckets). compute bucket = skein64(body) % 256. store as metric label fp_bucket.

liam: good. two more asks: 1) breakglass capture that bypasses deterministic sampling for a time window; 2) a way to request full captures for specific request-ids via support ticket.

clare: breakglass flow should require two approvers and write an immutable audit entry. UX: one-click "request breakglass" on a trace; approval happens in the modal.

roxana: from infra side, breakglass will temporarily set a capture override cookie for the tenant for 1 hour. we must emit an alert to #oncall and include audit_id.

paul: security note: any reversible storage must be enterprise-only and must require customer KMS. hosted cannot enable reversible decryptable PII. document this clearly.

liam: also need sampling edge performance numbers. benched redaction + hmac sampling vs. post-route sampling. initial microbench shows ~1.8ms extra p95 at edge for structured redactions + HMAC, which might be acceptable for low-volume tenants.

clare: rollout plan: feature flag in gateway, canary 0.5% tenants for 48h, telemetry check for gateway_p95, capture_success_rate, and "heatmap_fidelity" (new metric). expand to 10% then GA.

roxana: add rollback conditions: gateway_p95 increase >10% OR capture_success_rate drop >5% OR heatmap_fidelity drop >15%. console rollout dashboard will auto-evaluate these.

paul: small config example for routes.yaml:

```
- route: /v1/annotate
  sampling:
    type: deterministic-hmac
    key_ref: projects/redwood/keys/sampling-v1
    rate: 0.01
  redaction:
    mode: redact-edge
    rules: [email, phone, credit_card]
  reversible_storage: disabled
```

clare: QA note: ensure logs cannot accidentally include the pre-redaction body in error traces. add an assert in logging library to fail build if any log call includes raw_payload field.

liam: good call. also add unit tests for idempotent sampling across retries and for consistent behavior when tenant key rotates (older keys must be retained for grace period).

roxana: infra-bot scheduled INF-7820 for implementation. infra-bot: Created INF-7820 - "deterministic tenant capture + edge redaction + footprint metrics" https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-7820

paul: one final legal edge: EU DPAs sometimes require pseudonymization that is reversible under strict legal process. we'll add a reversible-mode flag that requires tenant_kms_ref and signed DPA approval before enabling.

clare: thanks team. I'll sketch the console mockups and upload to the RFC doc.

liam: thanks all — I'll compile notes into RFC draft and post tomorrow.
